items.title: SEC asks investment firms to prove they have access to shares in startups
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities and Exchange Commission has stepped up its examinations of firms behind so-called special purpose vehicles (SPVs) that claim to offer exposure to private company investments, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter. The SEC has been asking registered investment advisers for proof that their SPVs own or have exposure to the shares in private companies that they claim to, the Journal said. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: 'Please hold on': Wife's plea for missing firefighter in Nepal
items.summary: Our family misses you so much." That was the heartbreaking plea from a woman known as @azielashaharuddin on Threads, whose husband, senior Fire and Rescue Department officer Mohd Sani Harul, remains missing following the devastating floods in Nepal last Wednesday. Mohd Sani and another Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department officer, Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, are among 56 Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the devastating floods in Nepal's Rasuwa district.

items.title: Traders put strategy first
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's fast-expanding online trading community is increasingly choosing trading platforms based on strategy, market exposure and the flexibility needed to navigate rapidly changing market conditions, rather than simply on which system offers the most features. The guide said traders typically select platforms based on their experience, preferred trading style and the range of instruments they trade. "Traders often ask us which platform is 'better', but in practice the platform that works best is the one that aligns with your specific trading strategy and daily habits," JustMarkets said in a statement.

items.title: Economics of shared production
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The recent debate over whether Penang historically "belongs" to Kedah illustrates how easily discussions of federalism can conflate fundamentally different questions. Penang and Kedah are a good example. But Northern Malaysia's manufacturing ecosystem no longer ends at Penang's border.

items.title: Sarawak haze crisis: Kuching API hits 407, six areas in hazardous zone
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Six areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at the hazardous level as of 8 am today, with the Serian District Police Headquarters recording the highest reading at 408. Three areas in Sarawak recorded readings at the very unhealthy level – Mukah (234), Bintulu (232) and Samalaju (225). Forty-eight areas nationwide were reported to have moderate API readings.

items.title: Kelantan sultanate crown: an ageless local craftsman's creation
items.summary: Kelantan Sultan's Office Protocol Officer Mohamed Safaruddin Ismail said the idea for the crown was conceived by Sultan Ismail ibni Almarhum Sultan Muhammad IV, who ruled Kelantan from 1920 to 1944, and it was first used during his coronation ceremony on April 28, 1921. At the ceremony, Tengku Temenggung Abdul Ghaffar ibni Almarhum Sultan Muhammad II placed the crown on Sultan Ismail, making it part of the history of the Kelantan Sultanate. "During the reign of Almarhum Sultan Yahya Petra ibni Almarhum Sultan Ibrahim, 470 diamonds and 52 emeralds and rubies were added, while a further 721 diamonds and 44 emeralds were added during the reign of Almarhum Sultan Ismail Petra ibni Almarhum Sultan Yahya Petra," he said.

items.title: Dear Malaysia: Our shared beloved home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Selamat Hari Kebangsaan and Selamat Hari Malaysia , my dear fellow Malaysians. Each year, I reflected on the many challenges facing our beloved nation; our economy, education, corruption, political reforms, climate change, artificial intelligence and the rapidly changing world around us. Many of us become husbands and wives.

items.title: Local institutions extend buying streak to five weeks with RM200.5mil inflow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Local institutions extended their net buying streak on Bursa Malaysia to five consecutive weeks, recording net inflows of RM200.5 million last week, MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB) said. "Meanwhile, the retailers reverted to net buying after a week of net selling, recording RM165.5 million in net inflows compared with lower net outflows of RM42.0 million in the prior week," it said. It said foreign institutions extended their net selling streak to four consecutive weeks on Bursa Malaysia, recording RM366.0 million in net outflows last week.

items.title: AI data centres could double urban heat island effect
items.summary: Sahabat Alam Malaysia (SAM) president Meenakshi Raman said heat risks can occur even before data centre operations begin, as soon as forested areas are cleared for construction. This means forest loss alone, even before a data centre is built, is enough to elevate heat levels in the surrounding area," she said. She said Malaysia has yet to demonstrate that large-scale AI data centre developments fully account for risks related to temperature increases.

items.title: Trump: AI data centre opponents want US to be 'backwards and poor'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Monday attacked opponents of artificial intelligence data centres, saying they would end up "backwards and poor" and were helping rival China. A backlash against the energy-guzzling centres has become a surprise issue in November's US midterm elections, with Trump at odds with many Republicans. Trump said.

items.title: Fatal LPT1 accident: Four dead in 11-vehicle crash near Kuantan
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 1 — Four people were killed in an accident involving 11 vehicles at KM110 of the East Coast Expressway 1 (LPT1) from Lanchang towards Kuantan yesterday. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said the department received an emergency call at 10.44 pm. He said those killed were trapped in two vehicles.

items.title: Fast-fashion giant Shein set to open flat in Hong Kong market debut
items.summary: HONG KONG: Shares in fast-fashion giant Shein were set to open flat in their Hong Kong market debut on Tuesday, following numerous setbacks that have long delayed its listing and undermined the foundations of its business. Known globally for selling US$5 tops and US$10 dresses, Shein has been hit by tariff and duty changes in the US and Europe. In 2022, it was one of the world's most valuable start-ups, worth an estimated US$100 billion, but last week's initial public offering valued the company at about US$26.5 billion.

items.title: GOF seizes 6,000 smuggled Thai saplings worth RM300,000 in Rantau Panjang
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 6,000 plant saplings believed to have been smuggled from Thailand in Kampung Padang Licin here yesterday. GOF Battalion 8 personnel also arrested a 61-year-old local lorry driver during the inspection at 12.45pm. GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the seizure occurred after officers intercepted a lorry driven by the senior citizen under suspicious circumstances.

items.title: Brazil, US resume negotiations on Trump tariffs
items.summary: BRASÍLIA: Brazil has resumed talks with the United States over the steep trade tariffs imposed by Washington, the government in Brasilia said Monday. Washington in July imposed two new sets of tariffs on the Latin American giant, claiming unfair trade practices and use of forced labour, charging 25 per cent on some goods and 12.5 per cent on others. In a follow-up call Monday with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira and Trade Minister Marcio Elias Rosa reiterated Brazil's objections to the "discriminatory " tariffs, while adding that Brasilia was ready to continue talks.

items.title: Search for fisherman off Pulau Tenggol ends with no clues found
items.summary: DUNGUN, Sept 1 — The search and rescue (SAR) operation for fisherman Sabrie Rusli, 32, who was feared missing after his boat capsized in the waters off Pulau Tenggol near here last Thursday, was called off yesterday after no clues or discoveries were detected. Kemaman Maritime Zone Director Maritime Commander Abdul Halim Hamzah said the search operation for the fisherman covered an area of approximately 801.22 square nautical miles and was carried out systematically, taking into account weather conditions, sea states, currents, and the possibility of the victim drifting. “Throughout the operation, various search methods were implemented, including surface searches, the use of sonar, diving operations, and a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) to help detect any clues or objects believed to be related to the victim.

items.title: Malaysia Day address should bring further reforms for workers, small businesses, says Guan Eng
items.summary: “Anwar’s announcement that the annual sales threshold for exemption from mandatory e-Invoicing would be raised from RM1 million to RM3 million may disappoint those hoping for the threshold to be raised to RM5 million,” he said. Lim said the higher threshold would nevertheless benefit about 1.1 million MSMEs by exempting them from mandatory e-Invoicing requirements. Other measures cited by Lim included an increase in the school maintenance allocation from RM1 billion to RM1.5 billion next year, an additional RM200 million for hawkers and small traders, and RM1 billion to improve digital capabilities in public healthcare.

items.title: Asia's refined fuel imports hit post-war low, can the Middle East help?
items.summary: Asia's imports of light and middle distillates are estimated at 5.10 million barrels per day (bpd) in August, falling from 5.61 million bpd in July, according to data compiled by Kpler, a commodities analyst. Imports are down about 2.0 million bpd from the average of 7.06 million bpd in the three months leading up to February 28, when the US and Israel launched aerial strikes against Iran. Exports of light and middle distillates from the Middle East are estimated by Kpler at 2.14 million bpd in August, down from 2.58 million bpd in July.

items.title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz in 'extremely good shape'
items.summary: HAMILTON: US President Donald Trump said Monday that the Strait of Hormuz is in "extremely good shape," claiming US naval assistance has helped an average of 30 ships pass through each night, Anadolu Ajansi reported, "We have the Strait of Hormuz in extremely good shape. "Many, many ships got through last night. As you know, with the Navy's assistance, and we've been averaging 30 ships a night.

items.title: FKLI poised to test 1,700 support, says RHB Research
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI futures contract (FKLI) is poised to test the 1,700-point support level amid continued selling pressure, according to RHB Research. In a note, the firm said the FKLI fell 23 points to close at 1,700 points last Friday, after opening at 1,722.50 points and hitting an intraday high of 1,732 points before falling to a low of 1,693.50 points. "If selling pressure follows through, the FKLI may pull back towards 1,680 points.

items.title: Malaysia's manufacturing sector posts slight improvement in August: PMI data
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The seasonally adjusted S&P Global Malaysia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) posted above the neutral mark of 50.0 that separates growth from contraction for a third straight month in August. "The historical relationship between the PMI and official data indicates that gross domestic product and manufacturing output growth should improve in the third quarter of 2026," S&P Global said in a statement today. Nonetheless, S&P Global said sustained growth in new orders encouraged some firms to expand their payrolls; as a result, August marked the first rise in employment in four months, with manufacturers taking on both full- and part-time staff.

items.title: Fahmi hails behind-the-scenes heroes of National Day celebration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil expressed his highest appreciation and gratitude to all parties who worked tirelessly to ensure the success of today’s 2026 National Day celebration. “Your presence and spirit made this year’s celebration truly meaningful,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday. Happy National Day,” he said.

items.title: Bercham 10 fire: One hurt as major blaze damages nine factory lots in Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 1 — A man suffered burns to his body in a fire that spread to nine factory lots in Persiaran Industri Bercham 10, Bercham here yesterday. Perak Fire and Rescue Department asst operations director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the man, 42, suffered burns to one per cent of his body and received first aid from emergency medical rescue services (EMRS) on the scene after a team of seven fire engines and 40 personnel responded to the fire after a call at 3.36 pm. "The fire had started at a Class B plastics factory measuring 30 metres (m) by 13 m, which was 50 per cent burned, while other affected factories, Lot 10 and 11 suffered 20 per cent damage, Lots 12, 13 and 14 (70 per cent), Lots 16 and 18 (80 per cent), Lot 15 (10 per cent) and Lot 17 (60 per cent),” he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: Ringgit opens lower amid elevated US treasury yields
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened lower against the US dollar on Tuesday amid elevated US Treasury yields and uncertainty over the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest rate outlook, said an analyst. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the 30-year US Treasury bond yield has been rising persistently to 5.25 per cent, amid expectations that the Fed could maintain a cautious stance on interest rates at the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting on September 15-16. On another note, he said the ringgit is expected to remain cautious against the US dollar amid the resumption of military attacks between the US and Iran, which had pushed Brent crude prices higher to US$90.49 per barrel.

items.title: Two killed, four hurt in boat crash near Mersing jetty
items.summary: MERSING, Sept 1 — Two people died, while four others were injured in a two-boat collision near the Sungai Mersing estuary here last night. The Fire and Rescue Department’s (JBPM) Operations Control Centre reported receiving an emergency call regarding the incident at 9:04 pm. Following that, a Fire Rescue Tender and a Fire Response Vehicle (FRV) with a strength of nine personnel from the Mersing Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) were rushed to the Mersing Jetty.

items.title: MBPP cracks down on foreigners trading, slaughtering chickens
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) will take stern action against premises allegedly used by foreigners to trade and slaughter chickens, following complaints. MBPP mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the council had conducted enforcement operations against the premises several times, including sealing them for two weeks. One post claimed Team Surplus members had conducted an operation targeting foreigners along Jalan Macalister here ahead of National Day.

items.title: Sarawak haze worsens, Serian records hazardous API of 415
items.summary: KUCHING: Haze conditions in Sarawak have worsened, with five areas recording hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) levels, led by Serian at 415 as of 6am today. Four other areas recorded very unhealthy levels: Sibu (298), Mukah (228), Bintulu (221), and Samalaju (218). Meanwhile, four areas recorded unhealthy levels, led by ILP Miri at 184, followed by Miri (178), Kapit (176), and Limbang (166).

items.title: Unidentified body found in drain, police suspect murder
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH: The body of an unidentified man, believed to be a murder victim, was found in a drain along Jalan Industri 7 in Kampung Baru Sungai Buloh near here on Aug 29. District police chief Superintendent Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said police were alerted to the discovery by members of the public, and the Fire and Rescue Department was enlisted to assist in retrieving the body. He said the body was subsequently sent to the Sungai Buloh Hospital for a post-mortem examination.

items.title: Four killed in crash involving 11 vehicles near Temerloh
items.summary: TEMERLOH: Four people, including three family members, were killed and three others injured in an 11-vehicle crash at Km110.4 of the East Coast Expressway 1 (LPT 1) near the Temerloh toll plaza exit last night. The 10pm incident involved a tanker truck, an express bus, four cars, three sports utility vehicles (SUVs), a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), and a pickup truck. He said the crash also claimed the life of a man travelling in another SUV.

items.title: Rare black bass caught in Penang river after 15 years
items.summary: The Penang Fisheries Department said the catch on Aug 30 was significant as local fishermen had not reported seeing the species in the area for about 15 years. In a Facebook post, the department identified the fish as Lutjanus goldiei, a predatory estuarine species known for its strength and endurance, making it a prized sport fish. The department said the species was more commonly found in estuarine areas in Sabah and Papua New Guinea, making its presence in Penang noteworthy in terms of its geographical distribution.

items.title: Before the Sky Turns Grey
items.summary: El Niño is not one of them. We watch it developing across the Pacific - meteorologists track the oceans, weather agencies issue forecasts, plantation managers watch rainfall and farmers the sky. Yet when the land dries, fires break out and haze drifts across Southeast Asia, we still behave as though nature has surprised us.

items.title: US trade curbs put Malaysia's solar, semiconductor ambitions to the test
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The latest United States (US) trade measures on polysilicon pose risks for Malaysia's solar industry but could create opportunities for its semiconductor sector. The policy is aimed at strengthening US domestic manufacturing and reducing reliance on China in supply chains considered critical to solar panels, semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI) and energy security. According to Bernreuter Research, the proposed US minimum import price for polysilicon is US$21 per kilogramme (kg), while the current global polysilicon spot price is around US$4.78 per kg.

items.title: Bank Negara seen holding OPR on Thursday as global rate pressures build
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to keep the overnight policy rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75 per cent this week, with resilient domestic demand and manageable inflation giving it room to stay on the sidelines. UOB Global Economics & Markets Research expects Bank Negara to maintain its "wait-and-see" stance at its Sept 3 Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting while remaining vigilant over external developments. Bank Negara expects headline inflation to average between 1.5 per cent and 2.5 per cent this year.

items.title: AirBorneo weighs selling older ATRs ahead of fleet revamp in 2027
items.summary: KUCHING: AirBorneo Airways Sdn Bhd (AirBorneo) is considering phasing out its older ATR aircraft as the Sarawak-owned carrier prepares to renew its turboprop fleet in the second half of 2027. Chief executive officer, Megat Ardian Aminuddin, said the airline was examining several options for the aircraft that would leave its fleet. AirBorneo and turboprop manufacturer ATR announced an agreement during the Singapore Airshow 2026 for eight new ATR 600-series aircraft.

items.title: AirBorneo plans wider Asian network from Kuching hub
items.summary: KUCHING: AirBorneo Airways Sdn Bhd (AirBorneo) plans to develop Kuching as a network hub connecting Sarawak's rural and urban communities with Sabah, Kalimantan, Peninsular Malaysia and other regional markets. Chief executive officer Megat Ardian Aminuddin said passengers arriving in Kuching would be able to connect to other destinations across AirBorneo's network. AirBorneo currently operates Rural Air Services and other turboprop routes across Sarawak, Sabah and Labuan.

items.title: US Army Secretary Driscoll submits resignation: White House
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has submitted his resignation, the White House confirmed Monday, following reports of tensions with Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. Asked about a Wall Street Journal report that Driscoll had resigned, White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly did not deny it. "Driscoll has been highly effective in advancing President Trump's agenda to Make America Strong Again at the Department of the Army," Kelly said.

items.title: Trump vows to hit Iran hard after fresh exchange of fire
items.summary: ASHEVILLE, North Carolina: US President Donald Trump threatened further strikes against Iran on Monday after the first exchange of direct attacks in a month, raising tensions in a conflict that had recently shifted into an economic standoff. Iran launched missiles overnight at two US air bases in Jordan in response to a US attack on Iran's Larak Island, where Washington said it had struck Iranian launchers firing mines into the Strait of Hormuz. Iran called Trump's post "laughable."

items.title: Indonesia backs stronger Asean cooperation on transboundary haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesia has reaffirmed its commitment to the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP), describing it as an important framework for regional cooperation in tackling transboundary haze. He said Indonesia also continued to advocate accelerating the full operationalisation of the Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control to further strengthen regional coordination. The AATHP is a legally binding regional agreement adopted by Asean member states in 2002 to prevent, monitor and mitigate transboundary haze pollution arising from land and forest fires.

items.title: Malaysia open to Asean haze pact review [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is open to reviewing the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP) amid concerns that the bloc has yet to fully address the recurring haze problem. "The ministry recognises concerns over the recurring transboundary haze issue. The AATHP is a legally binding agreement adopted by Asean member states in 2002 to prevent, monitor and mitigate transboundary haze pollution arising from land and forest fires.

items.title: Not a ‘fast lane’: Miros tells Malaysian motorists to keep left, overtake right
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Think the right-most lane on a Malaysian highway is simply the “fast lane”? Director of the Road Safety Engineering and Environment Research Centre Rizati Hamidun said the left lane is generally meant for normal travelling and slower-moving vehicles, while the middle lane can be used for travelling and, where appropriate, overtaking slower vehicles in the left lane. The middle lane can be used by motorists travelling at moderate speeds and by vehicles overtaking slower traffic in the left lane.

items.title: Budi Madani: Restored RON95 quota, higher diesel allocation bring relief to motorists, traders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — The government’s decision to restore the assistance quota under the Budi Madani programme for RON95 petrol and increase the diesel quota has been well received by various layers of society and traders, considering it a timely step in alleviating the burden of living costs. In the address, he announced that the basic eligibility quota for RON95 petrol subsidies would be increased from 200 litres to 300 litres, while the Budi Diesel quota would be raised from 300 litres to 400 litres, effective today. Private sector worker, Furzani Ahmad, 24, said that the return of this quota contributed tremendously towards his commute to work.

items.title: College student dies after fall from Setapak condominium
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — An 18-year-old college student died after falling from the 22nd floor of a condominium in Setapak here this morning. Free Malaysia Today reported that Wangsa Maju police chief Annas Sulaiman said police were alerted at about 8.50am after a security guard found the student’s body at Residensi Teratai on Jalan Langkawi. Annas said the footage showed the student subsequently falling from a corridor on the 22nd floor to the sixth floor.

items.title: Mat Sabu: Malaysia needs rice self-sufficiency rate of at least 80pc for secure supply
items.summary: In another development, Mohamad said the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry wants to explore an approach to integrating giant freshwater prawn farming in rice fields to produce two sources of yield from the same agricultural area. He said he saw the potential of this approach during his visit to a rice field area that integrated rice cultivation with giant freshwater prawn farming China two weeks ago. “In that rice field, there are giant freshwater prawns, there are two yields, one from rice and one from prawns….the giant freshwater prawn fry were brought from Malaysia and breeding was carried out in China.

items.title: Haze worsens in East Malaysia as Sarawak records hazardous API, Sabah unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Haze conditions remained severe in East Malaysia today, with four areas in Sarawak recording hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm, while four areas in Sabah registered unhealthy levels by 6pm. Three other areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy readings, namely Sarikei at 277, Sibu at 243 and Mukah at 216. Meanwhile, Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic and Kimanis in Sabah recorded moderate API readings of 121 and 116 respectively, while 42 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings and three recorded good readings as of 4pm.

items.title: Malaysia seeks Nepal’s nod to deploy SMART team for flood SAR mission, says Tok Mat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Malaysia has sought permission from the Nepalese government to deploy the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) to assist in search and rescue (SAR) operations following the floods in the country. “The discussion focused on the latest developments in the SAR operations, particularly efforts to locate Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides in Nepal recently,” Mohamad wrote on his official Facebook page. On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was reported as saying that the Madani Government has decided to send the SMART Team to Nepal to assist with SAR operations following the flood disaster that hit the country.

items.title: MAHA 2026 attracts 1.8 million visitors, records RM6m sales in three days
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 31 — The Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026 has recorded 1.8 million visitors and nearly RM6 million in sales in its first three days, says Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. He said 184,000 vehicles were recorded entering and leaving the exhibition grounds during the period, reflecting heavy traffic due to the large turnout. “Three days have passed, and visitor turnout for MAHA has reached 1.8 million, with 184,000 vehicles moving in and out.

items.title: Three-year-old boy injured after foot run over by tow vehicle at Terengganu National Day parade
items.summary: The boy’s mother, Puteri Anis Athirah Wan Rosli, 36, from Cendering, said the incident occurred at about 9.45 am in front of Wisma Persekutuan here. She said her son, Che Ku Muhammad Khairul Amir Che Ku Mohd Khairul Azlan, fell before being run over by the tow vehicle carrying a Fire and Rescue Department boat. My son followed her.

items.title: AI programme to equip 100,000 youths for changing job market, says HR minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — The AI for the People Programme, which targets 100,000 youths aged between 18 and 30, is an important step towards preparing Malaysia’s workforce for rapid changes in the employment landscape, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan. He said access to artificial intelligence (AI) technology should be expanded among youth to ensure they possessed skills relevant to the needs of the current job market and were not left behind in global technologicl developments. “As such, providing 100,000 youths with access to AI technology is an important investment to equip Malaysian talent with relevant skills and ensure they are not left behind in the changing global job landscape,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Armizan: Political maturity key to keeping unity govt stable
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Political maturity and the awareness of balancing political rights with the responsibility of nation-building are important to ensure the stability of the Unity Government, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. In a Facebook post in conjunction with National Day today, he said the new political landscape of the country after the 15th General Election (GE15) needs to be accepted with the awareness that government stability is crucial in steering the direction of national development and the welfare of the people. He said the country’s new political landscape after the end of one-party dominance must be accepted by taking lessons from the experience between 2018 and 2022 which saw the change of three prime ministers and three Cabinet line-ups in one term.

items.title: King Charles conveys National Day message to Sultan Ibrahim, praises partnership and shared Commonwealth values
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — King Charles III and Queen Camilla have conveyed their congratulations to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and the people of Malaysia on the country’s National Day on Monday. In the message shared by the British High Commission in Malaysia, King Charles expressed confidence that the UK-Malaysia Strategic Partnership would provide a valuable opportunity to deepen cooperation between the two countries in trade, technology and other shared priorities ahead of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027. Meanwhile, King Charles also reflected upon the enduring partnership between the two nations, rooted in the shared values and mutual respect that define the Commonwealth.

items.title: Sabah CM Hajiji announces RM3,000 aid for each household hit by Kota Kinabalu fire
items.summary: Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the amount comprised RM1,000 contributions each from the state government, the federal government and the Yayasan Kebajikan Sabah. He said the state government would also assist efforts to rebuild the victims’ homes through coordination between the State Secretary’s Office and Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA). Hajiji said that on humanitarian grounds, each non-Malaysian KIR affected by the fire in the village would also receive RM1,000 in aid from the state government.

items.title: Family prays for Gelugor hiker missing in Nepal floods, Penang government ready to assist
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 31 — The family of Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, who has reportedly remained unreachable following flash floods and landslides in the Nepal-Tibet border area in Nepal last Wednesday, hopes that the hiker will be found safe. He said the family, who live in Taman Tun Sardon, Gelugor, here, were currently in Kuala Lumpur to follow developments concerning Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad, who works with the Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM) Penang, through Wisma Putra. “Yesterday, family members attended a meeting with Wisma Putra to obtain information about Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad, and until now, we have also not received any phone calls or messages from him in Nepal.

items.title: From midnight to noon, Hospital Tunku Azizah welcomes 12 Merdeka babies including twin girls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — As the nation celebrated its 69th National Day, 12 newborns, including a pair of twin girls, began their life stories at Hospital Tunku Azizah (HTA) here today. All ten ‘Merdeka babies’ were delivered between midnight and noon, comprising six baby boys and six baby girls. HTA director Dr Shamsul Anuar Kamarudin said a birth on National Day is not only a special date, but it also carries a deeper meaning as a symbol of life, hope and the nation’s future.

items.title: Nine students injured after school bus carrying 36 crashes in Sabah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Nine students from Sekolah Menengah (SM) Sains Sabah suffered minor injuries after a bus carrying 35 students and a teacher was involved in an accident on the Kota Belud-Kundasang road in Sabah this morning. Kota Belud Fire and Rescue Station chief Elge Bakuk said firefighters were dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call. “All the victims were later taken to Kota Belud Hospital for further treatment using ambulances from the Health Ministry in Tuaran and Kota Belud, as well as an ambulance from the Malaysian Civil Defence Force,” he said.

items.title: Customs sniffer dogs Goku and Cafrey join military K9s marching at Putrajaya National Day
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — While their daily routine involves tracking drugs at national entry points or performing military guard duty, K9 dogs Goku and Troy share a common mission today, namely marching alongside 33 other dogs at the National Day parade in Dataran Putrajaya. Johnson Pedro said that initial training for the parade involved walking the dogs individually before pairing them with compatible dogs to march side by side. “Military dogs are highly trained.

items.title: Suspect arrested after teen shot when hunting companion mistakes him for animal in Sarawak
items.summary: MIRI, Aug 31 — The shooting case involving a 17-year-old teenager in Long Lidong, Lawas, has been resolved with the arrest of a suspect on August 25, said Lawas district police chief DSP Liong Tindan. Liong said following the arrest of the suspect, the police also recovered a homemade firearm, locally known as a ‘ bakakuk ’, believed to have been used in the incident. “The police are continuing investigations, including tracing witnesses and gathering other information related to the case.

items.title: Kuskop to expedite disbursement of PM’s additional RM1b microcredit pledge, says minister
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 31 — The Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives (Kuskop) will expedite the disbursement of an additional RM1 billion in microcredit funds to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement yesterday. Minister Steven Sim said the increase in allocation brings this year’s total microcredit funding to RM6 billion, up from RM5 billion. Yesterday, Anwar, who is also finance minister, announced the additional RM1 billion in micro financing facilities and said the government had agreed to raise the e-invoice exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million annually.

items.title: Election Commission to reveal proposed new, renamed Sarawak state seats on Sept 1
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 31 — The names and locations of Sarawak’s 17 proposed new State Legislative Assembly (DUN) constituencies will finally be publicly unveiled by the Election Commission (EC) tomorrow (September 1). The announcement is eagerly anticipated as it will provide greater clarity on the proposed expansion of the Sarawak Legislative Assembly from 82 to 99 seats, following the redelineation exercise undertaken by the EC. Apart from the new seats, the EC has proposed renaming several existing seats.

items.title: Penang council seizes licensed dog after viral video shows attack on stray in Tanjung Bungah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Penang authorities have seized a licensed dog after a viral video showed it repeatedly attacking a smaller stray in Tanjung Bungah, with the incident now under investigation under the Animal Welfare Act 2015. According to The Star , the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) said it seized the dog today after receiving a complaint through its official WhatsApp channel yesterday over the incident at Pearl Hill. MBPP said checks found that the dog had a valid licence and was registered as a mixed breed.

items.title: ‘Ultraman’ detained near main stage ahead of Sultan Nazrin’s arrival at Perak National Day celebration, says state police chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — A man dressed as Ultraman was detained near the main stage at Perak’s National Day celebrations today after police said his behaviour appeared suspicious in an area where Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah and other members of the Perak royal family were due to be seated. According to Berita Harian , Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the local man, who is in his 40s, was detained at about 5am after he was seen entering and lingering near the main stage area. Also present were Raja Muda Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, Raja Di Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Idris Shah, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and members of the state executive council.

items.title: Malaysia Day 2026: Final prep meeting set for Sept 5 ahead of Kuching celebration, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — A meeting to review the final preparations for the 2026 Malaysia Day celebration in Kuching, Sarawak, will be held on September 5, ahead of the main event at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) on September 16. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the official celebration would take place on the night of September 16, with various side events lined up around BCCK and Plaza Merdeka to enliven the Malaysia Day festivities. Fahmi, who is also chairman of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) main committee, said he was confident that Malaysians from across the country would attend the event, which would feature an exhibition tracing the history of Malaysia’s formation.
